explanation: This pole is a nominal-boundary detector: it fires on the closed-class token that opens or separates the next nominal unit, not on the words of that unit. Its strongest responses are the delimiter between two same-category premodifiers of one head (a comma between two attributive adjectives of a noun, 1.56 mean over 70 scan cases and up to 3.26, and and/& between two proper names or initials in an author list), then referent-picking determiners that open a noun phrase (the, this/these, that, its/their, a/an, another, strongest after a preposition, conjunction, subordinator or transitive verb), then the comma/semicolon/period that closes one clause or sentence and starts the next; prepositions themselves, auxiliaries (a determiner directly after 'was'/'is' is dead), pronouns, quantifiers (all, some, more, most), every content word (nouns, verbs, adjectives, proper names) and non-delimiting punctuation (brackets, quotes, hyphens, apostrophes) are near zero.
